name: Trenbolone
lead: Trenbolone, often called tren, is a synthetic anabolic-androgenic steroid (AAS) of the nandrolone group. It is used in veterinary medicine as a growth promoter in cattle, usually as the acetate ester in implants, and it has never been approved for human medical use.[1] It is used non-medically by bodybuilders and other athletes who want more muscle mass, strength and a lean, vascular look.[1][2]

Its pharmacology is described as a potent androgen receptor agonist with strong anabolic activity and little conversion to oestrogen.[1] Published human research on trenbolone is almost entirely limited to reviews of adverse effects and to veterinary and environmental studies; no controlled human trial of its effect on muscle or appearance has been identified. A 2024 review concluded that trenbolone, like other AAS, is associated with frequent harmful effects, reporting that about 90 percent of users experience adverse effects.[2]
In looksmaxxing forums it is discussed both as a physique drug and, among very young users, as a supposed aid to bone growth, a claim for which no supporting studies were found.

paras: In livestock, trenbolone acetate is implanted under the skin of beef cattle to improve muscle gain, appetite and feed efficiency.[1] Early pharmacological work examined its combination with the oestrogen hexestrol for bull and heifer fattening and considered consumer exposure.[3] Studies of implants in steers and heifers continue to look at growth and carcass outcomes.[1]

In humans, trenbolone and its esters are obtained illicitly. Users cite muscle mass, strength, vascularity and reduced body fat as the aims, often at doses far above veterinary levels, according to an encyclopedic overview.[1] Reviews describe such use as common among amateur athletes and note that its popularity is increasing.[2]

sections.h: Appearance uses in physique and looksmaxxing culture
paras: Within bodybuilding and physique-focused appearance communities, trenbolone is discussed as a way to add muscle mass and strength and to lower visible body fat, producing the dense, hard, high-contrast look associated with stage conditioning. Proponents link the compound's lack of oestrogenic conversion to a 'dry' look with less subcutaneous water, which they treat as the chain from the drug to a sharper physique.[1][8]

Looksmaxxing forums place it among the physique and 'height' stacks discussed by younger members, usually alongside growth hormone or peptides, and the threads include both enthusiastic planning and replies warning about harms.[10][11] A 2026 clinical review names trenbolone among the unregulated injectable 'biohacking' drugs that physicians are being asked to recognise in patients pursuing cosmetic and athletic enhancement, and describes product contamination, inaccurate dosing and cardiovascular stress as potential risks.[9]

Trenbolone is a 19-nor derivative of testosterone with additional double bonds in the steroid ring (estra-4,9,11-triene). It is reported to bind the androgen receptor with around three times the affinity of testosterone and not to be aromatised to oestrogen or reduced to dihydrotestosterone.[1] Its strong activity at the receptor is consistent with older binding work using the related compound methyltrienolone as a high-affinity ligand in skeletal muscle and prostate.[4] An encyclopedic overview also reports high-affinity binding to the progesterone receptor.[1]

Esters such as acetate and enanthate are hydrolysed to the active free steroid after intramuscular injection, differing mainly in release rate.[1] In cattle, tissue residues are highest in liver and kidney, and metabolites include the 17-alpha and 17-beta epimers.[1]

Trenbolone is an estrane steroid and a derivative of nandrolone with two additional double bonds in the steroid nucleus, with the formula C18H22O2.[12] Its esters attach at the 17-beta position and include acetate, enanthate, hexahydrobenzylcarbonate and undecanoate; the esters are cleaved in the blood to release free trenbolone, and the reported half-lives of the esters differ, from about one to three days for the acetate to about eleven days for the hexahydrobenzylcarbonate.[12] It was first synthesised in 1963.[12]

Wikipedia notes that the often-quoted statement that trenbolone is five times as potent as testosterone traces to a single book, that rat data may overstate it, and that two reviews suggest about three times.[12] In a rat study, trenbolone raised androgen receptor gene expression at least as strongly as dihydrotestosterone, and the compound also binds the progesterone and glucocorticoid receptors.[12] Proposed muscle mechanisms include increased ammonium uptake by muscle, higher protein synthesis, appetite stimulation and reduced catabolism.[12] Studies conflict on metabolism: some show conversion by aromatase to oestrogenic compounds and others show conversion by 5-alpha-reductase to androgenic compounds, which means that the statement that tren does not convert is itself contested.[12]

Trenbolone was first synthesised in 1963.[12] The hexahydrobenzylcarbonate ester, sold under the brand names Parabolan and Hexabolan, was formerly used clinically in humans but is no longer marketed.[12] The acetate ester is used as a growth promoter in cattle, and agricultural research on implants spans decades, including 1970s work on combined hexestrol and trenbolone treatment of bulls and heifers and recent randomised trials in beef steers and feedlot heifers on implant dose and release pattern, adipogenic gene expression and performance.[3][13][14][15]

sections.h: Livestock use, regulation and the environment
paras: Steroidal implants have been used in the beef industry for more than 60 years, and trenbolone acetate is one of several hormones placed in small ear implants to increase daily gain through greater skeletal muscle growth.[17] A 2010 review notes that five hormones including trenbolone are legally used as implants in the United States, whereas the European Union bans all hormonal growth promoters in livestock and polices the ban through inspection programs, so the two regulatory systems differ sharply.[16]

Researchers have followed the compound through the farm environment. A 2001 study that treated cattle with trenbolone acetate and then measured dung, liquid manure and soil found that the trenbolone metabolite persisted through months of manure storage, with a half-life in liquid manure of about 267 days, and remained detectable in soil for up to 8 weeks after spreading; the authors recommended further study of endocrine-disrupting potential.[18] A three-year Nebraska survey found the highest androgenic activity in a feedlot retention pond and lower levels downstream, although instrumental analysis in that study did not detect significant trenbolone metabolites.[5] Laboratory exposure of fathead minnows to 17-beta-trenbolone reduced fecundity and altered endocrine function.[6]

Food-safety work has also looked at consumers. In a controlled trial, prepubertal pigs fed ground beef from cattle given steroid growth promotants did not show early onset of oestrus.[20] A 1990 study examined oestradiol, zeranol or trenbolone acetate implants and heifer puberty and fertility.[21]

Users and clinicians describe a sudden bout of coughing, lasting minutes, during or after injection of trenbolone, which Wikipedia says can occur with any oil-based steroid injected into a vessel and which has been linked to prostaglandin release and to bradykinin.[12]

Trenbolone is a Schedule III controlled substance in the United States, Schedule IV in Canada, Class C in the United Kingdom (with no penalty for personal possession), and a crime to possess or use without prescription in Australia, and it falls in the C5 anabolic-steroid class in Brazil.[12] Athletic and bodybuilding use is illegal in the United States, several European countries and several Asian countries.[12]

No studies found of trenbolone given to humans in a controlled trial for muscle, fat loss or appearance. Published literature consists of reviews of adverse effects in users,[2] veterinary studies of implants in cattle,[1][3] and environmental work on trenbolone residues in feedlot runoff, which has been associated with androgenic activity in water bodies[5] and with reduced fecundity and altered endocrine function in fathead minnows exposed to 17-beta-trenbolone.[6]

A 2024 review of trenbolone's effects on organs reported that severe acne and gynaecomastia affect roughly one third of users, and that excessive body hair, stretch marks, hypertension and cardiac arrhythmia are also seen. It also reported effects on the nervous, reproductive and immune systems, and local problems from injection including inflammation, fibrosis, nerve damage and, rarely, necrosis, with the added problem of contaminated products.[2]

An encyclopedic overview also describes a cough after injection, night sweats, insomnia, anxiety and aggression, and suppressed natural testosterone production.[1] A broader review of sudden cardiac death in AAS users documents cardiac mechanisms for deaths associated with these drugs as a class.[7]

A 2020 case report in the journal Medicine describes delirium associated with anabolic steroid use, one of several reports of neuropsychiatric effects in AAS users as a class.[19] The 2026 review of unregulated injectables adds that products sold outside regulated channels may be contaminated or inaccurately labelled, so an individual's exposure can differ from what the label states.[9]

Trenbolone is a Schedule III controlled substance in the United States and is prohibited in sport under anti-doping rules.[1] Its use in cattle is regulated separately, and the United States is described as allowing trenbolone acetate for that purpose.[1]

On T Nation, users have described it as a 'monster steroid' that gives a dry, hard look rather than water retention.[8] On looksmax.org there are many threads of users, some in their teens, posting about tren cycles, plus threads asking about low doses.[10][11]

timeline.event: Pharmacological review considers growth promoters in cattle, including trenbolone plus hexestrol.[3]
The European Union bans hormonal growth promoters in livestock production, while the United States continues to permit trenbolone acetate implants.[22]
Study traces trenbolone metabolites through cattle manure and soil.[18]
Studies report androgenic activity in feedlot-affected waters and effects in fathead minnows.[5][6]
Review of organ effects reports high rates of adverse effects among users.[2]
A clinical review names trenbolone among unregulated injectable looksmaxxing drugs.[9]

lore.intro: On looksmax.org tren is discussed as a strong physique drug and, by some very young posters, as something that might help bone growth or height; other users reply with warnings.[10][11]

claims.claim: Low-dose tren helps bone growth and final height.
claims.believers: A poster proposed a microdose of trenbolone because it 'activates satellite cells' and might act on mesenchymal stem cells relevant to final height, combined with growth hormone and BPC-157.[11]
claims.experts: No published studies were found showing that trenbolone increases adult height in humans. Responding users on the forum were sceptical, with one warning a 14-year-old that it would not help bone and risked health.[10]

claims.claim: Tren gives a dry, hard physique without water retention.
claims.believers: Forum users describe tren as non-oestrogenic and producing a 'granite dry' striated look sought by bodybuilders.[8]
claims.experts: The compound is reported not to aromatise to oestrogen,[1] but no controlled human trial has measured its effect on body composition.

claims.claim: Tren is safe enough at low doses or for teenagers.
claims.believers: Teenage posters on looksmax.org share cycles and ask for ratings, treating it as a routine part of a stack.[10]
claims.experts: A 2024 review reports adverse effects in about 90 percent of users, including acne, gynaecomastia, hypertension, arrhythmia and injection-site complications.[2]

claims.claim: Tren is a staple of the looksmaxxing injectable scene alongside peptides.
claims.believers: Forum users discuss tren in the same threads as growth hormone and BPC-157 when planning physique and height projects.[11]
claims.experts: A 2026 clinical review lists trenbolone among unregulated injectable "looksmaxxing" drugs and describes contamination, inaccurate dosing and cardiovascular stress as potential risks.[9]

claims.claim: Tren mood effects: users report irritability and insomnia as part of the experience.
claims.believers: Users in physique communities commonly describe sleep disruption and a more aggressive mood on the compound as expected trade-offs.[8]
claims.experts: A 2024 review and an encyclopedic overview list anxiety, aggression and insomnia among reported psychiatric effects,[1][2] and a 2020 case report describes delirium associated with anabolic steroid use.[19]

claims.claim: Beef from implanted cattle exposes eaters to trenbolone.
claims.believers: Opponents of livestock hormones cite implants as a reason for concern about meat and water.[16]
claims.experts: US regulators permit trenbolone acetate implants with residue limits, while the EU bans hormonal growth promoters; a 2014 trial feeding ground beef from implanted cattle to prepubertal pigs found no early onset of oestrus.[16][20]

card.summary: A potent veterinary-origin steroid used for a dry, hard physique; no human trials, and reviews report adverse effects in most users.
card.note: Not approved for humans; controlled in the US and banned in sport; contaminated products reported.

quick.overview:
Trenbolone is a synthetic steroid used in cattle to promote muscle growth. It has no human approval, but bodybuilders and some looksmaxxers use it to gain muscle and get a lean, vascular look.

No controlled human trials of its effect on muscle or appearance were found. What exists is mostly reviews of side effects and veterinary work. Forum claims that it helps bone growth or height are untested.
quick.mechanism: It binds the androgen receptor strongly, reportedly more so than testosterone, and is not converted to oestrogen. Anabolic effects in muscle are inferred from animal work and user reports rather than human trials.
quick.risks: A 2024 review reports adverse effects in about 90 percent of users, including acne, gynaecomastia, hypertension, arrhythmia, psychiatric effects and injection-site damage. It is a controlled substance in the US and prohibited in sport.
